venue.name: Ladysmith Gallery
venue.description: The Ladysmith Gallery is a single street level exhibition room at Unit 7, 32 High Street in downtown Ladysmith. It is the exhibition space of the Arts Council of Ladysmith and District, which is catalogued separately, and it keeps its own address, phone number and email. A new show opens every month, mostly member shows drawing on artists from Vancouver Island and the Gulf Islands, and everything hung is for sale alongside a boutique of smaller local pieces. The gallery is open seven days a week from 10 am to 4 pm. Nothing on the site describes a school visit, a daycare visit, a guided tour or a group rate.
venue.address: Unit 7, 32 High Street, Ladysmith, BC V9G 1A1
venue.hours_notes: Open seven days a week, 10 am to 4 pm. Opening times can change on the days a show is being taken down and rehung, and closures are announced on their social media rather than on the website, so it is worth ringing first.

programs.name: Self guided gallery visit
programs.description: The gallery is open to the public seven days a week from 10 am to 4 pm, with a new exhibition every month. The September 2026 show is a member show called We Are All Connected, holding painting, photography, fibre art, linocut, stained glass, weaving and ceramics. Every piece is priced and for sale, and a boutique carries smaller local works. The site does not describe a group booking, a group rate, a guided tour or anything laid on for children, so a visit is simply walking in during opening hours.
programs.what_children_do: Walk into one long room off the main street and look at the month's show, which is paintings and photographs hung along the walls and small sculptures set on plinths. There is nothing to handle and nothing to make. Everything is priced and for sale.
programs.our_note: This is one room, not a building, so it is a twenty minute stop rather than a morning out. The work is hung at adult height and all of it is for sale, so it suits a group that can look without touching. Ring the gallery number before you set off, because the doors can be shut on the days between one show and the next.
programs.practical_summary: Nothing at all is published about washrooms, somewhere to eat, parking or step free access, and no admission price is given either. All of that has to be settled on the phone.
programs.evidence: All artworks in our online gallery are available for purchase at our Ladysmith Gallery during the show dates.

images.alt: A white clapboard building on a street corner with a black hanging sign reading Ladysmith gallery above a glass door, a wall sign reading Temperance, and a wide display window.
A long narrow gallery room with a dark plank ceiling and track lighting. Framed paintings hang in a row down one white wall and small works sit on white plinths at the far end.

gaps: No admission price is published anywhere. The site never says whether it costs anything to walk in, so that is the first thing to ask.

No school visit, daycare visit, guided tour or group rate is published. Searching the site for school, group and tour returns nothing to do with visiting, so a group visit would have to be arranged by phone or email with the gallery.
No youngest age, group size limit or how far ahead to ring is published.
Whether the gallery has a washroom, anywhere to leave coats or bags, step free access at the door, or anywhere nearby to park a bus is not published. It sits in a shopfront on High Street.

The children's art classes on this website belong to the Arts Council of Ladysmith and District, not to the gallery. They run at the council's classroom on Oyster Bay Drive and are booked through education@ladysmitharts.ca. They are recorded in the separate Arts Council of Ladysmith and District entry and have deliberately not been copied here.
The council also rents the gallery to its own members for ten day private shows at $925 to $1,100 a slot. That is an artist renting wall space, not a group visit, so it is not recorded as a program.

COORDINATES: the contact page publishes two Google Maps embeds. The one for the gallery carries a map centre of 48.994165, -123.820904 and a place link whose pin is 48.9941671, -123.8182497. The pin is the value used here, because that is the pattern that marks the place rather than the map view.

The Open Graph image for the gallery pages is a black and white wordmark rather than a photograph, so it was skipped. The main picture here is the exterior shot the gallery page uses as a background image.
The gallery gives a 604 area code phone number while the council office gives a 250 number. Both are published side by side on the contact page and are for different places.
